parts.title: A week without social media
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last month my cousin told me I spent too much time on my phone, and I laughed. Then she challenged me to stay off social media for a whole week, and I said yes before I could change my mind.

On the first day I kept picking up my phone to check things that were not there. I looked at the screen on the bus, in the queue at the shop, even in the middle of conversations. By Wednesday I was checking much less, and the week felt easier. I read half a book, which I had not done for months, and I cooked a proper dinner instead of watching videos while I ate.

The hardest part was not the free time. It was the messages. My friends use a group chat to plan everything, and I missed an invitation to a birthday meal because nobody phoned me. When I told them, they were surprised and a little sorry. We agreed that anything important would be sent to me by text as well.

At the end of the week I did not delete my accounts. I like seeing what my friends are doing, and I use the internet to learn new things. But now I put my phone on silent in the evening, and I leave my phone in another room when I go to bed. I am not sure my cousin was completely right about me, but I sleep better than I used to.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer accept the challenge?
options: She wanted to spend more time with her cousin.
She agreed quickly without thinking much.
She had already decided to leave social media.
questions.explanation: She says she said yes before she could change her mind, so she agreed quickly.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel by Wednesday?
options: She was bored with her free time.
questions.explanation: By Wednesday she was checking her phone much less and the week felt easier.

questions.prompt: What problem did she have with her friends?
options: They were angry about the challenge.
They stopped using the group chat.
questions.explanation: She missed an invitation to a birthday meal because nobody phoned her.

questions.prompt: What did her friends agree to do?
options: Send her important news by text too.
questions.explanation: They agreed that anything important would be sent to her by text as well.

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel about social media now?
options: It is useful if she controls it.
She should stop using it completely.
It is the main reason she cannot sleep.
questions.explanation: She kept her accounts because she likes them, but she puts her phone on silent in the evening.

parts.title: A town app for bus times
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Hartwell is a small town with a big problem: the buses never seem to come when the timetable says they will. Passengers used to stand in the cold, not knowing whether the number 12 had already gone. [1] Last spring, a group of students from the college decided to change that.

They started by sitting at bus stops and writing down the real arrival times for six weeks. [2] With that information, they built a simple app that shows where each bus is on a map.

The app was ready by September, but the students needed help from the bus company. [3] He liked it at once and agreed to share the live position of every bus.

The app went live in November. [4] The students say that the best comments come from older passengers, who now stay at home until the bus is nearly at their stop.

Of course, the app is not perfect. Sometimes the signal is weak and the map shows a bus in the wrong place. [5] The team reads every report and fixes problems within a few days.
sentences: They discovered that many morning buses were ten minutes late or more.
Most of them had never written a computer program before.
Users can report these mistakes with one button.
Some of them gave up on the bus completely.
Within a month, more than a thousand people had downloaded it.
So they asked to meet the manager and show him a first version.

gaps.explanation: “Some of them” refers to the passengers who stood in the cold, and the next sentence moves on to the students who wanted to “change that”.
After writing down real arrival times, the students discovered that buses were late; “that information” in the next sentence refers to this discovery.
They needed help from the bus company, so they met the manager; “He” in the next sentence is the manager and “it” is the first version of the app.
“Within a month” continues from “went live in November”, and “it” is the app. The next sentence talks about comments from users.
“These mistakes” refers to the bus shown in the wrong place, and “every report” in the next sentence links to the report button.

I looked at several websites to [2] prices and found two I liked. There was a special [3] on laptops that week, so I went to the shop on Saturday. I paid by card, and the laptop was [4] to my house two days later. It was easy to set up, and the battery [5] much longer than my old one. I am really [6] with it.

questions.prompt: Gap 5

parts.title: A message about a video call
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Chase,
Thanks for your message. Sorry I [1] answer the call yesterday evening. I was [2] the train and the signal was very weak. Can we try again on Sunday? I never wake up early on Sundays, so any time [3] ten o’clock is fine for me. Please remember to [4] on your microphone, because last time I could not hear you [5] all. If it still does not work, we can just send voice messages [6] of talking live.
Bye for now,
Tyler

gaps.explanation: A past action that did not happen needs a negative past form: “Sorry I didn’t answer”.
We say “on the train” for being a passenger on public transport.
He never wakes up early, so any time after ten o’clock suits him.
“Turn on” or “switch on” a microphone means to start it.
“Not … at all” is a fixed phrase meaning “not in any way”.
“Instead of” means “in place of”: voice messages in place of talking live.

parts.title: An interview with a web designer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Aaliyah, you design websites for small businesses. How did you start?

turns.speaker: aaliyah
turns.text: At school I made a website for my brother’s football team, just for fun. I didn’t think of it as a job, but then other parents asked if I could make one for their shops. So I started working on them after lessons and at weekends.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do you do first with a new customer?

turns.speaker: aaliyah
turns.text: I listen. Many people arrive with a long list of ideas, but when I ask what they want visitors to do, the answer is usually very simple: find the opening hours, see the prices, or send a message. So I begin by deciding what visitors need most.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What is the most common mistake?

turns.speaker: aaliyah
turns.text: Too much text. People read on their phones, often while they are walking, so short sentences and big buttons work much better than long paragraphs. Also, a page must load quickly. If it takes more than a few seconds, most visitors simply leave.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Has your job changed since you started?

turns.speaker: aaliyah
turns.text: A lot. Now there are tools that let anyone build a basic page, so some people say my job will disappear. I don’t think so. People still want someone who understands their business and can give advice. What I do now is more like teaching than designing.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What advice would you give to someone who wants to do this work?

turns.speaker: aaliyah
turns.text: Start with a small real project for someone you know. Don’t wait until you feel ready, because you learn most by finishing things. And look at websites you like and ask yourself why they work.

questions.explanation: She says “Too much text” is the most common mistake.
